data.name: Rule_social_contributions
data.value: The final contributions of a self-employed person in main occupation, owed on the year's net taxable professional income: one rate up to a first ceiling, a lower rate up to a second ceiling, nothing above it, and never less than the contribution on the minimum income. The social insurance fund bills them in four equal quarters, each rounded to the cent. The contributions lower the very income they are computed on, so the two are solved together.

data.name: Rule_flat_rate_costs
data.value: A director who does not prove real professional costs deducts flat-rate costs: a percentage of the pay left after the social contributions, up to a yearly maximum. They lower the taxable income and are never paid out.

data.name: Rule_taxable_income
data.value: Gross pay less your own social contributions and the flat-rate costs. It is never below zero.

data.name: Rule_income_tax
data.value: The progressive scale applied to the taxable income, less the reduction for the tax-free amount, gives the State tax. The federal government keeps that tax less the autonomy factor, and Wallonia adds its regional tax on the federal share. Each of the two is rounded to the cent, and the income tax is their sum.

data.name: Rule_municipal_surcharge
data.value: Your municipality's rate applied to the income tax, that is the federal share plus the Walloon tax.
